title: New York Deploys $360 Million for Stony Brook and Regional Hubs Supported by $1.37B in Federal Foundry Commitments - Quantum Computing Report
gist: New York's FY2027 budget commits $360 million to quantum: $300 million for a Quantum Research and Innovation Hub at SUNY Stony Brook (150,000 sq ft, with a hybrid quantum data center targeted for 2029) and $60 million for up to four regional commercialization hubs. This is layered on September 2026 CHIPS Act awards of $1 billion to Anderon (matched by $1 billion from IBM) for a 300mm superconducting quantum foundry in Albany and $375 million to GlobalFoundries' Quantum Technology Solutions in Malta.

insights.claim: New York's FY2027 state budget enacted a $360 million quantum allocation. It includes $300 million for a flagship Quantum Research and Innovation Hub at SUNY Stony Brook, with a planned 150,000-square-foot facility and the state's first university-hosted hybrid quantum data center targeted for 2029, plus $60 million for up to four Regional Quantum Technology Commercialization Hubs.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: State money is concentrating on infrastructure and data-center capacity, a potential procurement source for hardware vendors that supply hybrid quantum data centers.
insights.locator: Governor Kathy Hochul and Empire State Development

insights.claim: NYSTAR will run the selection of the four regional quantum commercialization hubs, focusing on open-access test facilities, startup incubation and shared technical resources that link regional hardware clusters with commercial end users.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Hub awards are an upcoming catalyst for regional quantum startups and test-facility operators in New York.

insights.claim: CHIPS and Science Act awards finalized in September 2026 include $1 billion for Anderon, matched by $1 billion from IBM, to establish an open 300mm superconducting quantum foundry at NY Creates' Albany NanoTech Complex.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A $2 billion open superconducting foundry could lower fabrication barriers for superconducting-qubit companies and strengthen IBM's ecosystem position.
insights.locator: The state capital package aligns with major federal awards

insights.claim: GlobalFoundries' Quantum Technology Solutions unit in Malta, New York received a $375 million CHIPS award.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: GlobalFoundries (GFS) gains federally subsidized exposure to quantum fabrication, a small but strategic growth vector.
insights.locator: alongside a $375 million award for GlobalFoundries

insights.claim: The combined state and federal commitments aim to connect New York's upstream hardware, semiconductor and cryogenic assets with downstream enterprise demand in financial services, defense and healthcare.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: New York is positioning itself as a full-stack quantum cluster, which matters for where companies locate and where talent and capital pool.
insights.locator: Together, the state and federal commitments

insights.claim: New York's cryogenics base includes Bluefors in Syracuse, described as a major North American dilution-refrigerator production footprint, and SEEQC in Elmsford, which manufactures commercial cryogenic Single Flux Quantum (SFQ) control chips.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Cryogenics and control electronics are picks-and-shovels suppliers that benefit whichever superconducting qubit vendor wins.

insights.claim: In Rochester, the AIM Photonics 300mm test, assembly and packaging facility for silicon photonics is supported by a $321 million Department of Defense agreement.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: DoD-backed photonics packaging capacity supports photonic and optical quantum suppliers.

insights.claim: On Long Island and in NYC, a 161-mile quantum networking testbed links Stony Brook and Brookhaven National Lab, and Qunnect has demonstrated commercial entanglement swapping over 17.6 km of NYC fiber.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Metro-scale entanglement swapping is an early marker of commercial quantum networking readiness.

insights.claim: IBM Quantum's Poughkeepsie site is the main assembly and fleet data center for IBM's superconducting processors, and IBM's Starling fault-tolerant system is targeted for 2029.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: 2029 for IBM Starling is a key fault-tolerance milestone that investors can track against IBM's roadmap execution.
insights.locator: Full Systems & Compute Access (value chain table)

insights.claim: Downstream demand in the NYC metro is at the early proof-of-concept stage: certified randomness at JPMorganChase, bond trade fill optimization at HSBC with IBM, and oncology imaging at MSKCC.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: End-user demand is still at PoC stage, so near-term quantum revenue comes mainly from government and infrastructure spending, not enterprise production workloads.
